summary: Odd credit reversal showing on finalized invoice after hourly postback tag reclassification during dedicated failover
description:
Issue summary:
Customer NexusAI reports a credit reversal line on their finalized invoice for billing period ending 2026-02-28. The reversal correlates with a subset of hourly postbacks that were reclassified during a dedicated failover window on 2026-02-27 22:40 UTC.

Impact:
- Customer received a negative adjustment (credit reversal) of ~USD 1,420 on finalized invoice INV-2026-02-28-NA which they did not expect.
- Their internal finance team flagged the adjustment and paused autopay pending clarification.
- Customer workloads are on Dedicated; they are concerned credits may be incorrectly applied to parent org cost center.

Environment:
- Dedicated pool: dp-nyc-3 (us-east region)
- Private keys: customer-dedicated-key-nyc (no access to customer data)
- Services involved: postback-processor v3.12, hourly-accumulator v2.4, billing-aggregator v1.9

Steps to reproduce / observed pattern:
1) During failover on 2026-02-27 22:35-22:50 UTC, dedicated pool rerouted residual traffic to hosted fallback for ~12m.
2) Postback-processor emitted hourly postbacks tagged with temporary tag "dedicated-fallback-nyc" which later underwent a tag-normalization job on 2026-02-28 03:12 UTC.
3) Billing reconciler applied a postback reclassification that grouped those postbacks under a reserved-hour smoothing rule.
4) Final invoice shows a reversal line titled "Hourly buffer reclassification credit reversal" for amount -1,420.00 USD tied to tag dedup key prefix dfb-nyc-20260227.

Logs / evidence attached in links:
- Billing reconciliation trace: https://console.redwood/prod/billing/traces/trace-82f3
- Postback debug window (anonymized) snapshot: https://console.redwood/prod/psnap/ps-20260227-2240 (redacted)
- Slack thread: https://redwood.slack.com/archives/C0123456/p1677491200000

Investigation notes so far:
- Billing engineering checked reconciler logs; the reclassification job marked 3,812 hourly postbacks as "warmup-buffer" then a downstream compaction pass removed what it considered duplicate warmup credits. This compaction incorrectly converted previously-applied provisional credits into a reversal on the finalized invoice line.
- Metering team observed tag-shadowing: temporary tag deduped into parent org tag due to a mismatch in namespace normalization rules introduced by PR 8b7c3a2.
- Reproducer: replaying the exact postback subset in staging replicates the compaction behavior and produces a negative adjustment in the aggregator staging invoice.

Customer requested outcome:
- Immediate hold on autopay until resolved.
- A clear explanation of the cause and a correction entry on the next billing cycle (or immediate manual credit).
- Confirmation that future dedicated failovers will not trigger the same reclassification behavior.

Next steps planned:
- Billing eng (Diego) to open hotfix to skip compaction for postbacks tagged with "dedicated-fallback-*" by 2026-03-11 EOD.
- Metering to add a normalization test asserting namespace isolation between temporary fallback tags and reserved-hour tags.
- Support to coordinate manual credit/adjustment for NexusAI pending engineering fix and to provide timeline to customer.

Requested from customer (already provided):
- Sample invoice (INV-2026-02-28-NA) and internal cost-center where the reversal was observed (provided).
- Confirmation they paused autopay (provided).

Remarks:
- This ticket spans billing reconciliation, meter normalization, and dedicated routing logic. We should track as high-priority until corrected on ledger and applied as a manual adjustment or patch that prevents recurrence.
